cells.rationale: No byte-range locks, no rename operation at all (no rename/Rename in pkg/api/controller.go or pkg/catalog/catalog.go — only CopyObject+DeleteObject, non-atomic), and no live shared filesystem, so cross-pod sqlite/git cannot work (lakectl local even warns it breaks on case-insensitive FS, cmd/lakectl/cmd/local.go:34-37); what it does ship is a genuinely enforced O_EXCL-equivalent — If-None-Match:"*" create-exclusion accepted on API upload (controller.go:3560-3578), presigned-link completion (controller.go:1033-1044), gateway PUT (gateway/operations/putobject.go:409-422) and multipart complete (postobject.go:113-126), backed by KV CAS — plus the atomic branch-head commit CAS (graveler.go:2289-2379). Enterprise delta: the Everest NFS/FUSE mount that would make this axis meaningful is not in this repo.
cells.vs_lean: 0.5 above Lean's 1: Lean has no cross-client primitive at all between checkouts, while lakeFS's exclusive-create is server-enforced across every client population.

cells.rationale: Through the primary surfaces (OpenAPI + S3 gateway) another client's uncommitted write is visible essentially immediately: reads resolve staging token first (graveler.go:1768-1847), staged writes are a durable KV put acked before the HTTP response, DynamoDB reads use ConsistentRead:true (kv/dynamodb/store.go:241), and branch gets are only micro-batched ≤3ms (config/defaults.go:162-169) with caches confined to immutable commits (10min) and repo records (5s). Variance: lakectl local is snapshot-until-explicit-pull against a pinned at_head commit (pkg/local/index.go:16-51, diff against idx.AtHead in local_commit.go:116-117), i.e. Lean-grade ~1.5 for that front end; the enterprise mount is not scoreable here.
cells.vs_lean: Well above Lean's 1.5 because every server-mediated reader sees staged writes at once; only the checkout-style lakectl-local front end degrades to Lean's snapshot posture.

cells.rationale: What exists is enforced refusal, not detection: the condition is evaluated inside StagingManager.Update's read-modify-write with KV SetIf on the staged key (graveler.go:1900-1932, staging/manager.go:117-136), mapped to 412 ErrPreconditionFailed, and it binds all writer populations that traverse lakeFS — API upload, presigned link, gateway PUT and multipart complete — multi-instance-safe on any KV backend. But the vocabulary is half-missing: If-Match on objects returns ErrNotImplemented (pkg/api/apiutil/conditions.go:21-23, only If-None-Match "*" is accepted), and the Commit API takes no expected-head (controller.go:3381-3402), so replace-if-unchanged exists only for settings objects (SetBranchProtectionRules checksum CAS, graveler.go:803-807). Out-of-band bucket writers are bound by nothing.
cells.vs_lean: Matches Lean's enforcement quality (refusal/serialization, stronger than flint's load-weak detection) but loses 0.5 vs Lean's 4 because object-level If-Match update is simply not implemented.

cells.rationale: There is no local write-back tier: an acked PUT means the blob is already durable in the object store (WriteBlob completes at controller.go:3600 before CreateEntry at :3644-area/1044 and the response) and the staged entry is a durable KV put (staging/manager.go:101-115 kv.SetMsg), so an acked write survives loss of the entire lakeFS server fleet on postgres/dynamo backends; commits are content-addressed and inert until the final branch CAS, so crashes leave only harmless dangling objects (ref/manager.go:623-634). Held back from 5 because uncommitted namespace entries live in a second failure domain (KV — the badger "local" backend is single-node), and the lakectl-local front end's uncommitted edits are bare files with no journal (order Sync→Commit→WriteIndex, local_commit.go:178-228), which is Lean-grade ~1 for that variant.
cells.vs_lean: Far above Lean's 1.5: Lean acks into a node-local write-back tier before publish, while lakeFS's ack already implies object-store + KV durability.

cells.rationale: The documented branch-per-writer posture gives real arbitration: commits serialize through a non-retried seal CAS plus a retried head CAS (graveler.go:2289-2379, retryBranchUpdate :2417-2446), merges are true three-way per-key with refusal on conflict (ErrConflictFound, committed/merge.go:329-371) or explicit dest-wins/source-wins strategies, and a dirty destination is refused (ErrDirtyBranch, graveler.go:1476-1494) — the second writer is serialized or refused-with-surfaced-conflicts. On one shared branch, though, same-key staged writes are blind last-writer-wins (unconditional Set is a plain kv.SetMsg, staging/manager.go:112-115) and an unscoped commit sweeps every staged change on the branch including a concurrent writer's half-finished files (the reason lakectl's hasExternalChange guard exists, local_commit.go:36-80).
cells.vs_lean: A full point above Lean's 2.5: branch isolation plus serialized commits and conflict-refusing merges is a stronger arbiter than Lean's checkout lease, despite the same-branch LWW hole.

cells.rationale: An out-of-band write into the repo's storage namespace is invisible to the catalog (reads resolve only cataloged xid addresses, upload/path_provider.go:101-106), and the uncommitted-GC design explicitly scans the bucket and deletes objects "not referenced by lakeFS" (design/accepted/gc_plus/uncommitted-gc.md:18-25,53), so a foreign object is silently garbage-collected rather than surfaced; a foreign overwrite of a tracked physical address is served without verification, with the stale stored checksum still presented as the ETag (gateway/operations/getobject.go:153). The only foreign-data pathway is the deliberate import flow — there is no detection of unexpected writes to a live tree.
cells.vs_lean: The mirror image of Lean's 4: Lean's inbox preserves and surfaces foreign S3 writes, while lakeFS ignores them, serves corrupted bytes undetected, and its GC eventually deletes them.

proposal.dimension_note: lakeFS lands well above flint's Lean column on the server-mediated axes — acked writes are already in S3+KV (4.5 vs 1.5), branch/merge machinery genuinely arbitrates (3.5 vs 2.5), and API/gateway readers get read-after-write freshness (3.5 vs 1.5) — because it replaces a filesystem with a KV-CAS-serialized commit store. It pays for that on the filesystem-shaped axes (no locks, no rename, no shared sqlite/git; 1.5) and is the exact inverse of Lean on foreign writes: unreferenced out-of-band objects are silently served-corrupt or GC-deleted, never surfaced (1 vs 4). Everest mount (NFS/FUSE write mode) is enterprise and absent from this repo, so nothing here restores the filesystem axes.

verdicts.reason: Every citation verified: If-None-Match "*" create-exclusion is genuinely enforced via KV insert-if-absent (pkg/graveler/staging/manager.go:117-136 SetMsgIf; graveler.go:1902-1932 handleUpdate) on API upload (pkg/api/controller.go:3560-3570), presigned completion (~:1033), gateway PUT (pkg/gateway/operations/putobject.go:332-358), multipart complete (postobject.go:113-126). Grepped pkg/api, pkg/catalog, pkg/gateway for Move/Rename — no rename op exists, only CopyObject+DeleteObject. Case-insensitivity warning at cmd/lakectl/cmd/local.go:33. No byte-range locks or shared fs anywhere in repo; 1.5 vs Lean's 1 is the right gap for one enforced primitive.

Verified: Get resolves staging+sealed tokens before committed (graveler.go:1786-1810 getFromStagingArea, Get :1810+); DynamoDB ConsistentRead:true (pkg/kv/dynamodb/store.go:241,516); graveler.max_batch_delay=3ms, commit cache 10min (immutable commits only), repo cache 5s (pkg/config/defaults.go:155-170). Probed for a hidden branch-head cache — none; branch reads go through the 3ms batcher only. lakectl local pins at_head (pkg/local/index.go AtHead; local_commit.go:116-121 diffs against idx.AtHead). Server-mediated readers see staged writes immediately; the variance note for lakectl local is accurate.

Verified both halves: enforcement is real (condition evaluated inside StagingManager.Update read-modify-write with SetMsgIf predicate, staging/manager.go:117-136; kv.ErrPredicateFailed→ErrPreconditionFailed, graveler.go:1892-1894; under a create race the KV insert-if-absent arbitrates, so refusal not detection) and the vocabulary gap is real (If-Match→ErrNotImplemented, pkg/api/apiutil/conditions.go:22-23; If-None-Match only "*"; Commit body has no expected-head, controller.go:3381-3403; checksum CAS exists only for branch-protection rules, graveler.go:799-807). 3.5 = Lean 4 minus the missing object-level If-Match is exactly right.

I attacked the one hole that could refute 4.5 — async metarange upload — and it does not exist: sstable writer Close calls fh.Store synchronously (pkg/graveler/sstable/writer.go:153) which runs pyramid tier_fs.go store()→adapter.Put (tier_fs.go:232) before Commit's branch CAS, so acked commits have their ranges in the object store. WriteBlob completes before entry+response on API (controller.go:3600 area) and gateway paths; staged entries are durable kv.SetMsg (staging/manager.go:112-115); addCommit is content-addressed SetMsgIf, inert until branch CAS (ref/manager.go:623-634). The 0.5 deduction for single-node badger KV and lakectl-local bare files is legitimate.

Verified: seal via non-retried BranchUpdate CAS then retried head CAS (graveler.go:2289-2308, retryBranchUpdate :2417-2446); merges refuse per-key conflicts (committed/merge.go:117,146,201,325 ErrConflictFound) and refuse dirty destination (graveler.go:3154); same-branch staged Set is unconditional kv.SetMsg LWW (staging/manager.go:112-115); hasExternalChange guard confirmed (local_commit.go:36-80). Checked graveler.branch_ownership (defaults.go:172+) — defaults false and addresses commit contention, not the staged-write LWW hole, so it can't push the score up. 3.5 between NFS 5 and Lean 2.5 fits the branch-per-writer posture.

Verified: cataloged addresses are xid-generated under a data prefix (upload/path_provider.go:101-106), so foreign objects are invisible to reads; design/accepted/gc_plus/uncommitted-gc.md states objects found in the namespace listing but absent from committed/uncommitted listings 'can be safely deleted' — foreign writes are GC'd, not surfaced; GET serves the stored entry.Checksum as ETag with no verification of fetched bytes (gateway/operations/getobject.go:153, same on the range path), so a foreign overwrite of a tracked physical address is served corrupt and undetected. No detection mechanism exists anywhere in the repo; 1 vs Lean's inbox-preserving 4 is the correct mirror.

cells.rationale: Primary documented data posture is presigned-direct: OpenAPI GetObject with presign=true 302-redirects to a store URL and the client helper parallelizes 8MB ranged GETs at concurrency 10 (pkg/api/helpers/download.go:26-27,198-254), so warm reads run at S3/NIC-native throughput with no lakeFS on the byte path; the S3-gateway variant proxies every byte through the server via BlockStore.Get + io.Copy (pkg/gateway/operations/getobject.go:134-141,170) with no data cache anywhere (pyramid caches only committed sstables, pkg/pyramid/tier_fs.go), which is a full tier lower, while a lakectl-local checkout reads native local files.
cells.vs_lean: Lean's 5 is warm data on local NVMe with zero network on the read path; lakeFS still crosses the network to S3 per read (or worse, through the proxy).

cells.rationale: Presign staging moves upload bytes entirely off the server — GetPhysicalAddress mints a stateless HMAC-signed address plus presigned PUT (pkg/api/controller.go:892-948, pkg/catalog/catalog.go:3234-3292) and S3-only presigned multipart covers large objects (pkg/block/s3/adapter.go:488-519) — so the app writes at raw S3 PUT/multipart throughput but blocks until S3 acks every byte; the gateway variant streams the body through the server behind an MD5+SHA256 hashing reader (pkg/upload/write_blob.go:20-34), and presigned multipart does not exist on GCS/Azure (gs/adapter.go:782-784, azure/adapter.go:689-691).
cells.vs_lean: Lean's 5 acks at local disk and publishes in the background; lakeFS's app-visible write path is network-bound to the object store end to end.

cells.rationale: Every created object costs an HTTPS round trip + auth (20s/1024-entry cache, pkg/config/defaults.go:66-68) + one KV staging SetMsg (pkg/graveler/staging/manager.go:101-115) + a backing-store PUT of its own object — and lakectl local commit replays a storm per-file (presigned PUT + LinkPhysicalAddress each, default parallelism 25, cmd/lakectl/cmd/root.go:165), so a node_modules-sized tree is hundreds of thousands of HTTP round trips with no batched manifest; it beats per-op NFS because creates are lock-free and embarrassingly parallel against a stateless server, but stat/delete storms are still one server RT each (graveler Get = staging KV get + pyramid-cached sstable lookup, pkg/graveler/graveler.go:1787-1847).
cells.vs_lean: Lean's 5 runs the storm natively and publishes as a batched manifest; lakeFS pays per-file HTTP+PUT at sync/API time with no content dedupe (fresh xid address per upload, pkg/upload/path_provider.go:101-106).

cells.rationale: A lakectl-local checkout is plain local files with literally nothing on the I/O path between explicit commands — sync workers only run at clone/pull/commit/checkout (pkg/local/sync.go:74-97) and the only local state is the .lakefs_ref.yaml pointer (pkg/local/index.go:16-51) — so sqlite transactions, git, and build dirs run at native disk latency. Front-end variance: the S3 gateway/OpenAPI front ends cannot admit these loops at all (scored under Workload envelope), and the enterprise Everest mount is not in this repo.
cells.vs_lean: Equal to Lean's 5 and for the same reason — the hot loop touches only the local filesystem; lakeFS is if anything more absent (no sidecar process at all during the loop).

cells.rationale: The workspace posture requires `lakectl clone` to fully materialize the prefix before it is usable — the in-repo warning says so outright ('requires a full local copy of cloned data', cmd/lakectl/cmd/local.go:36) and there is no lazy/partial fetch in OSS (that is enterprise Everest) — softened by 25-way parallel presigned downloads with 8MBx10 ranged GETs per large file; pure API/gateway access is instant first-byte with no clone step at all (auth + first GET), and the server itself warms fast since the pyramid sstable cache persists across restarts (pkg/pyramid/tier_fs.go:110-147).
cells.vs_lean: Matches Lean's 3 — same full-checkout-before-usable shape, O(working set) at object-store throughput — with the API front end as an instant-access variance Lean lacks.

cells.rationale: Servers are stateless (all mutable state in pluggable KV; branch updates are pure CAS via SetIf, pkg/graveler/ref/manager.go:452-484) and with presigned-direct data the aggregate byte path is client-to-S3, so throughput scales with the object store, not lakeFS; the shared caps are the KV store (postgres single 100-partition table, pkg/kv/postgres/store.go:48-50) and per-branch commit serialization via CAS retry (BranchUpdateMaxTries=10 then ErrTooManyTries, pkg/graveler/graveler.go:53-54), blunted by the 50k/10min commit cache and 3ms batch executor (pkg/config/defaults.go:158,169).
cells.vs_lean: Equal to Lean's 4: both push data-plane scale onto S3 itself, and both keep a serialization point per branch/tree (Lean's barrier vs graveler's per-branch commit CAS); gateway-proxy deployments cap lower at server NICs.

cells.rationale: The object-API side admits data-lake-scale shapes flint cannot — working set and unpublished dirty set are effectively unbounded (a staged entry is one KV row, pkg/graveler/staging/manager.go:101-115; commits copy unchanged ranges by reference, pkg/graveler/committed/merge.go:73-85) — but no OSS front end offers shared-RWX, multi-pod sqlite/git, append, rename, or partial overwrite, and POSIX workloads exist only via a full local copy the repo itself labels non-scalable (cmd/lakectl/cmd/local.go:36); the mount that would widen this (Everest, NFSv3/FUSE) is enterprise and absent from this repo.
cells.vs_lean: Half a point above Lean's 2: same no-shared-RWX, local-disk-bounded POSIX story, but the S3/OpenAPI face additionally admits unbounded object workloads Lean's node-disk checkout cannot.

proposal.dimension_note: lakeFS lands as a near-Lean profile with the peaks shaved off: presigned-direct data paths and stateless servers put streaming and scale-out one network hop behind Lean's local-NVMe 5s (3.5/3.5/4), lakectl local exactly matches Lean's native hot-loop 5 and full-checkout cold-start 3, but per-object HTTP round-trips with no batched manifest hold metadata storms to 2.5 against Lean's 5. Its one relative win is envelope (2.5 vs 2): the object API admits unbounded working sets, though every POSIX shape still requires a full local copy the repo itself calls non-scalable — the mount that would change that is enterprise and not in this codebase.

verdicts.reason: Verified download.go:25-27 (8MB parts, concurrency 10) and downloadPresignMultipart:162-234; gateway proxies via BlockStore.Get + io.Copy (getobject.go:136,170) with no object-data cache (pyramid tier_fs caches only committed range/metarange files). Also found the gateway itself can 302-redirect presigned when the client advertises s3RedirectionSupport (getobject.go:47,120-131), reinforcing presigned-direct as primary posture. Every warm re-read still pays S3 across the network — 3.5 below FUSE's cached 4 and Lean's local-NVMe 5 is correct.

Verified controller.go:892-948 (GetPhysicalAddress + presigned PUT), catalog.go:3286-3293 HMAC-signed stateless address, S3-only presigned multipart (s3/adapter.go:488-519; gs/adapter.go:783 and azure/adapter.go:690 return ErrOperationNotSupported), and the gateway's hashing proxy (upload/write_blob.go:20-34). App-visible path blocks until S3 acks every byte — 3.5 between sys NFS (3) and write-back FUSE (4), below Lean's local-ack 5, holds.

Verified auth cache 20s/1024 (defaults.go:66-68), staged entry = one KV SetMsg (staging/manager.go:101-115), defaultParallelism=25 (root.go:165), per-file presign+LinkPhysicalAddress in the upload helper (helpers/upload.go:383,424-434), fresh xid per upload so no content dedupe (path_provider.go:104). Lock-free 25-way-parallel creates beat serial NFS storms (sys 1.5) but each file is 2-3 HTTPS RTs + its own PUT with no batched manifest — 2.5 below FUSE's 3.5 and Lean's 5 stands; the lakectl-local native-storm argument is offset by the app-blocking per-file commit sync, a half-point quibble at most.

Verified sync workers run only inside explicit Sync/clone/commit/checkout calls (local/sync.go:74-97) and the only persistent local state is the .lakefs_ref.yaml pointer (local/index.go:16-19,39-51) — a checkout is plain local files with no process on the I/O path, equal to Lean's 5; API/gateway inadmissibility is correctly priced under Workload envelope.

Verified the in-repo full-local-copy scalability warning (cmd/lakectl/cmd/local.go:35, localScalabilityWarning pointing to the enterprise mount docs), 25-way parallel sync with presigned/ranged downloads (sync.go + download.go), and pyramid cache re-adoption across restarts (tier_fs.go:110-147 handleExistingFiles). Same O(working set)-at-object-store-throughput shape as Lean's 3.

Verified stateless per-branch CAS: BranchUpdate = getBranchWithPredicate + kv.SetMsgIf (ref/manager.go:452-484), BranchUpdateMaxTries=10 (graveler.go:53-54), postgres DefaultPartitions=100 (kv/postgres/store.go:48-50), commit cache 50k/10min and 3ms max_batch_delay (defaults.go:158-169). Presigned data plane scales with S3; KV + per-branch commit CAS are the caps — 4, equal to Lean's 4, is right.

Verified a staged entry is one KV row (staging/manager.go:101-115), merges copy unchanged ranges by reference (committed/merge.go:73-85 writeRange), no OSS front end offers shared-RWX/append/rename/partial overwrite (S3 whole-object semantics; mount is enterprise and absent), POSIX exists only via the full local copy the repo itself warns about (local.go:35), and concurrent lakectl-local writers get ErrConflict (sync.go:128-129). 2.5 = Lean's 2 plus the unbounded object-API face is well supported.

cells.rationale: Every write path demands per-request cryptographic proof: the S3 gateway fully verifies SigV4 (canonical request, constant-time hmac.Equal at pkg/gateway/sig/v4.go:209 and sig.go:121-123, 15-min clock skew, streaming chunk signatures) with no anonymous fallback (sig.go:118), and the OpenAPI server chains JWT/basic/cookie/OIDC/SAML plus presigned-STS AWS-IAM login (pkg/api/auth_middleware.go:87-160, pkg/api/controller.go:820-889). Docked for long-lived static access keys as the primary credential and the OSS default (rbac=none) collapsing to one superAdmin identity (pkg/auth/basic_service.go:18-23,109-117); presigned-direct variance: after issuance the backing store accepts the 15-min URL signature alone.
cells.vs_lean: Above Lean's 3 — per-request SigV4 signing plus federated login options beats a static bearer posture, though still below krb5p's mutual Kerberos 4.

cells.rationale: Native TLS exists but is opt-in (cmd/lakefs/cmd/run.go:307-311; BaseConfig.TLS pkg/config/config.go:458-462) and the shipped default is cleartext HTTP on 0.0.0.0:8000 (pkg/config/defaults.go:10) with cookie Secure only when TLS is on (pkg/api/serve.go:62-68); SigV4 gives header+payload integrity even over plaintext, and the presigned data plane rides HTTPS to S3/GCS/Azure. Documented production posture is TLS (native or LB-terminated), but nothing refuses or warns on cleartext, and TLSSkipVerify/InsecureSkipVerify knobs exist (pkg/config/config.go:158, pkg/block/s3/adapter.go:197).
cells.vs_lean: Half a step under Lean's 4: equivalent TLS ceiling once configured, but Lean doesn't ship a cleartext default listener.

cells.rationale: Auth middleware rejects gateway and API requests before handlers touch bodies, errors are masked, and setup is one-shot 409 (pkg/api/controller.go:5565+), but /metrics and /_pprof/ are mounted unauthenticated on the service listener itself (pkg/api/serve.go:104-110; pkg/httputil/endpoints.go:25-40 exposes CPU-profile and heap endpoints any reachable peer can hammer), the OpenAPI body validator runs outermost — before AuthMiddleware — buffering JSON bodies pre-auth (pkg/api/serve.go:73-84) with no MaxBytesReader or rate limiting anywhere in pkg/, and each bogus gateway request costs a KV credential lookup.
cells.vs_lean: Below Lean's 4: a userspace Go server avoids kernel-NFS state exhaustion, but unauthenticated pprof/metrics on the data port and pre-auth body parsing are exposures Lean's authenticated-only surface doesn't have.

cells.rationale: The repo/object-granular ARN policy engine and its enforcement points are genuinely shipped (pkg/auth/service.go:1230-1327, ~115 authorize sites, gateway RequiredPermissions, list filtering pkg/auth/policy_filter.go), but no shipped backend can scope principals per repository: rbac=none is one all-powerful superAdmin (pkg/auth/basic_service.go:109-117), the only in-repo auth server grants ACLs with Resource="*" across ALL repositories (contrib/auth/acl/permission.go:29,41-60), and repo-scoped RBAC is enterprise/external (pkg/auth/build.go:14-35 fatals without an external endpoint). Worse, StageObject needs only fs:WriteObject yet links any regex-valid physical address — including another repo's storage namespace, readable via the server's own credentials — so even policy-scoped writers can reach across namespaces (pkg/api/controller.go:3704-3749).
cells.vs_lean: Far below Lean's 4: Lean enforces per-project bucket/prefix tenancy at the proxy, while this repo ships either no boundary or all-repo grants plus a cross-namespace StageObject primitive; enterprise RBAC would close most but not the StageObject gap.

cells.rationale: A compromised pod holds a long-lived static access key that in the shipped backends is either the omnipotent superAdmin credential (basic mode, max 1 user/1 key, pkg/auth/basic_service.go:18-23) or an all-repository ACL grant (contrib/auth/acl/permission.go:29), and its JWTs live 7-14 days with no per-token revocation in OSS (ClaimTokenIDOnce is ErrNotImplemented, pkg/auth/basic_service.go:476-478). Containment is fast once acted on — credential/user deletion propagates within the ~20s+3s auth cache TTL (pkg/config/defaults.go:66-69; JWTs re-resolve the user per request, pkg/auth/user_auth.go:11-23) and presigned URLs are single-object 15-min capabilities (pkg/api/controller.go:928-948) — but the gained scope is broad; enterprise scoped policies + STS principals would shrink it materially.
cells.vs_lean: Well below Lean's 4.5: Lean's pods carry short-lived scoped credentials, whereas lakeFS-OSS pods carry static keys that are all-repo or all-everything; only the 20s revocation propagation keeps this above flint sys.

cells.rationale: Auth configuration fails closed: missing auth.encrypt.secret_key refuses startup (pkg/config/config.go:681 validate:required), rbac modes without an external auth server Fatal (pkg/auth/build.go:14-35), ambiguous basic-auth migration Fatals with instructions (build.go:50-64), setup is one-shot, secrets are log-elided via SecureString (pkg/config/types.go), quickstart's well-known key and THIS_MUST_BE_CHANGED_IN_PRODUCTION secret bind only under explicit flags (pkg/config/defaults.go:19-52), and per-backend presign kill-switches exist. Against that: TLS-off/0.0.0.0 default with silent cleartext, unconditionally unauthenticated pprof/metrics (pkg/api/serve.go:104-110), and one shared symmetric secret doing triple duty (credential encryption via scrypt N=512, JWT signing, session cookies — pkg/auth/crypt/encryption.go:46-53, pkg/auth/token.go, pkg/api/serve.go:59) so one leaked config value forges every identity.
cells.vs_lean: One step under Lean's 4: comparable fail-closed startup validation, but Lean lacks the cleartext-default wire, the open diagnostics endpoints, and the single-secret-to-rule-them-all coupling.

proposal.dimension_note: lakeFS lands close to flint Lean on the front of the house — real SigV4/OIDC authentication (3.5 vs 3) and near-parity wire protection (3.5 vs 4) — but falls sharply behind on the multi-tenant axes because this repo ships the policy engine without a policy backend: OSS is one superAdmin or all-repo ACL grants, StageObject lets any writer graft foreign storage-namespace objects into its own repo, and pods hold long-lived static keys (tenancy 1.5 vs 4, blast radius 2 vs 4.5). Unauthenticated pprof/metrics on the service port and a cleartext-default listener also pull DoS (2.5 vs 4) and misconfiguration resistance (3 vs 4) below Lean; per-repo RBAC and mount are the enterprise deltas that would move mainly the tenancy and blast-radius cells.

verdicts.reason: Every cite verified: V4Verify builds the canonical request, signs, and compares via hmac.Equal (pkg/gateway/sig/v4.go:192-212), ChainedAuthenticator returns ErrMissingFields with no anonymous path (pkg/gateway/sig/sig.go:100-118), gateway middleware does per-request credential lookup + Verify + user resolution (pkg/gateway/middleware.go:26-80), and the API chain covers jwt/basic/cookie/oidc/saml (pkg/api/auth_middleware.go:87-160). The docks are also real: basic mode is a single superAdmin identity with MaxUsers=1 (pkg/auth/basic_service.go:18-23) behind long-lived static keys. One nuance the rationale omits — the gateway chain also accepts legacy SigV2/JavaV2 (HMAC-SHA1, middleware.go:37-41) and ExternalPrincipalLogin is gated off unless an external auth service + external principals are configured (controller.go:6521-6524) — but neither defeats a 3.5: per-request signing still beats Lean's static-bearer 3, and mutual-Kerberos krb5p at 4 stays above.

Verified: TLS is opt-in at serve time (cmd/lakefs/cmd/run.go:306-311), default listen is cleartext 0.0.0.0:8000 (pkg/config/defaults.go:10), cookie Secure is tied to TLS.Enabled (pkg/api/serve.go:62-67), and skip-verify knobs exist (pkg/config/config.go:458 TLSSkipVerify; pkg/block/s3/adapter.go:195-197 InsecureSkipVerify, though the latter is named SkipVerifyCertificateTestOnly). SigV4 header+payload integrity over plaintext and the HTTPS presigned data plane are real compensations. Whether the cleartext default costs 0.5 or 1.0 below Lean's 4 is a taste call with the same code on both sides — no evidence defeats 3.5.

Verified: /metrics and /_pprof/ are mounted unauthenticated on the service router (pkg/api/serve.go:105-107) with no config gate anywhere (grep over pkg/config and cmd), and ServePPROF exposes CPU profile, trace, and heap to any reachable peer (pkg/httputil/endpoints.go:25-45); the OpenAPI body validator is first in the chi middleware chain, before AuthMiddleware (serve.go:73-84), and grep finds zero MaxBytesReader/rate-limiter anywhere in pkg/ or cmd/; each bogus gateway key costs a KV GetCredentials (pkg/gateway/middleware.go:49). Mildly mitigating (and consistent with 2.5 rather than lower): ReadHeaderTimeout is set to 1 minute (run.go:283-285) and auth rejects before handlers run. 2.5 — equal to flint sys, below Lean's 4 — stands.

Every cite verified: the ARN policy engine with Deny precedence is real (pkg/auth/service.go:1230-1327 CheckPermissions), but basic-mode Authorize is unconditional Allow for the one superAdmin (pkg/auth/basic_service.go:109-117), the ACL model carries only a Permission with no repository list (pkg/auth/model/model.go:147-149), contrib ACL statements grant permissions.All across every repo (contrib/auth/acl/permission.go:28-29,40-70), rbac defaults to none (pkg/config/defaults.go:76) and non-basic modes Fatal without an external auth server (pkg/auth/build.go:14-35). The StageObject cross-namespace primitive checks out: fs:WriteObject only, PhysicalAddress validated against a generic per-scheme regex (DefaultValidationRegex, pkg/block/namespace.go:203) not the repo namespace, and normalizePhysicalAddress classifies out-of-namespace addresses as Full and stores them (controller.go:3704-3784, 1068-1080). 1.5 vs Lean's proxy-enforced 4 is right.

Verified: static access keys resolve to superAdmin (basic) or all-repo ACL grants (contrib), JWT login duration defaults 7d/max 14d (pkg/config/defaults.go:73-74), ClaimTokenIDOnce returns ErrNotImplemented in the shipped basic service (pkg/auth/basic_service.go:476-478), revocation propagates within the 20s+3s auth cache TTL (defaults.go:66-69) because UserByToken re-resolves the user per request (pkg/auth/user_auth.go:11-23), and presigned URLs are 15-min single-object (DefaultBlockstoreS3PreSignedExpiry, defaults.go:31; GetPhysicalAddress controller.go:893-948). Broad gained scope + fast-but-coarse revocation lands 2, between FUSE's 1.5 and krb5p's 3.5, well under Lean's 4.5. Confirmed.

The rationale's positive that known-bad secrets 'bind only under explicit flags' is defeated for one secret: blockstore.signing.secret_key defaults to the publicly-known constant OVERRIDE_THIS_SIGNING_SECRET_DEFAULT unconditionally in ALL modes — pkg/config/defaults.go:107 sets it in setBaseDefaults outside the quickstart/local switch (constant at defaults.go:23) — validation only requires non-empty (ValidateBlockstore, pkg/config/config.go:570-573), and no startup warning exists (run.go warns only for local blockstore type, run.go:130-131; grep finds no other reference). That key is the HMAC that makes link-address verification an integrity gate on four write paths (pkg/catalog/catalog.go:3234-3268; controller.go:336,412,516,585), so the shipped default is a forgeable second layer that silently degrades instead of refusing — the axis's exact failure mode. Stacked on the three counters the scorer already found (cleartext 0.0.0.0 default, pprof/metrics unconditionally mounted with no disable knob per serve.go:105-107, one symmetric secret doing credential-encryption/JWT/cookie triple duty), four independent silent-insecure defaults put lakeFS 1.5 under Lean's 4, not 1: 2.5, still above krb5p's 2 and a point over flint sys on the strength of genuinely fail-closed startup validation (validate:required config.go:681, build.go Fatals, one-shot setup, SecureString elision pkg/config/types.go:52-57).

proposal.dimension_note: lakeFS beats flint's Lean column on most Day-2 axes because the OSS system is a stateless multi-tenant service: a repo is KV rows plus an object-store prefix, so there is no per-share process to fail, roll, park, or wake, and clients fail with HTTP errors rather than wedged mounts. The costs are concentrated in three places: the shared KV store is an operated database whose outage is fleet-wide (and whose loss forfeits staged pointers and auth), reclaiming deleted bytes requires an operator-scheduled external Spark GC job per repo, and observability is per-operation rather than per-repo — the "is this share healthy/clean, what is its RPO" question has no shipped fleet surface, and /_health is a static string that ignores KV state.

cells.rationale: Failures present as HTTP errors, never client-kernel hangs: the OSS repo has no mount (Everest NFS/FUSE is enterprise, out of repo), object bytes are durable in the object store at upload time and committed metadata as immutable range files, so total server loss stops the data plane without losing durable state; startup is fail-fast (kv.Open/ValidateSchemaVersion logger.Fatal, cmd/lakefs/cmd/run.go:89-98). Deductions: the shared KV is a fleet-wide blast radius whose loss forfeits staged/uncommitted pointers, refs, and auth (staged entries are single kv.GetMsg records, pkg/graveler/staging/manager.go:78-99), and /_health is a static "alive!" (pkg/httputil/endpoints.go:16-23) while the DynamoDB checker only logs at debug (pkg/kv/dynamodb/store.go:601-609), so an LB cannot evict a dead-KV replica; esti has zero restart/failover/chaos legs (grep across esti/*_test.go = 0).
cells.vs_lean: Above Lean's 3.5: errors instead of hangs and nothing per-share to recover, but the central KV outage is fleet-wide where Lean's failures are per-share.

cells.rationale: Shared-nothing stateless replicas coordinate only via KV CAS (SetIf, pkg/kv/store.go:88-104), so a roll is a plain deployment restart: KV schema is validated at every boot (run.go:95-98), `lakefs migrate up` exists (cmd/lakefs/cmd/migrate.go:129-159), graceful shutdown is 30s (run.go:48), the pyramid committed-metadata disk cache rescans and re-registers itself after restart (pkg/pyramid/tier_fs.go:110-147 handleExistingFiles), and gateway multiparts persist in a KV partition across restarts (pkg/gateway/multipart/tracker.go). 249 releases over 6 years (CHANGELOG.md) show a proven cadence; the deduction is the mandatory treadmill — SECURITY.md supports only the latest release — and single-binary coupling of API+gateway.
cells.vs_lean: Well above Lean's 3.5: a mature stateless roll with no client remount ceremony, versus Lean's sidecar/barrier restart choreography.

cells.rationale: Thousands of repos cost zero per-repo standing compute — one server pool plus one KV database serves them all; per-instance (not per-repo) coordination is a 5s task heartbeat (pkg/catalog/catalog.go:89, 2273-2296) and an off-by-default correctness-optional branch-ownership lease (pkg/distributed/mc_owner.go:18-46, defaults.go:171). The recurring counterweight is GC: the server only writes prepare listings under _lakefs/retention (pkg/graveler/retention/garbage_collection_manager.go:23-27); mark/sweep is the external Spark job (clients/spark/.../gc/GarbageCollection.scala) the operator must schedule per repo, budgeted ~3h for a 20M-object repo (design/accepted/gc_plus/uncommitted-gc.md Bottom Line), plus the KV itself is an operated database.
cells.vs_lean: Above Lean's 3.5 on standing objects (no per-share CRs/sidecars at all) but carries a Spark GC fleet burden Lean does not have.

cells.rationale: The surface is service-level, not per-share: API and gateway Prometheus histograms are labeled by operation ID and status code only, with no repository dimension (pkg/api/metrics_middleware.go:15-41, pkg/gateway/stats.go:8-14); /_health is static and checks neither KV nor blockstore (pkg/httputil/endpoints.go:16-23); per-branch cleanliness exists only as a scripted per-repo DiffBranch API call (pkg/api/controller.go:3448), and the staged-pointer RPO exposure (KV backup posture) is surfaced nowhere per repo. Rich audit fields attach only under advanced/RBAC auth — an enterprise-side feature (pkg/httputil/logging.go:95-113, defaults.go rbac=none); default-on telemetry goes to the vendor (stats.enabled=true, defaults.go:126), not the operator.
cells.vs_lean: Half a point under Lean's 3: excellent /metrics + pprof for the service, but the axis's per-share health/clean/RPO question is unanswered where Lean at least has per-share manifests/status.

cells.rationale: The primary posture needs nothing installed or privileged: any stock S3 SDK works against the gateway (per-request Host/SigV4 dispatch on one listener, cmd/lakefs/cmd/run.go:283-298), and lakectl — including lakectl local checkout/clone/commit/pull/status (cmd/lakectl/cmd/local_*.go) — is one unprivileged static binary; presign mode additionally needs only object-store reachability (pkg/api/helpers/upload.go:382-447, pkg/local/sync.go:160-214). Variance: presigned multipart is S3-only (only s3/adapter.go sets PreSignSupportMultipart) and proxied mode routes bytes through the server. Enterprise delta: the POSIX mount (Everest, FUSE/NFS with client privileges) is not in this repo.
cells.vs_lean: A full point above Lean's 3.5: no per-pod sidecar, kernel module, or CSI at all — the trade is that OSS offers no filesystem semantics, priced under other dimensions.

cells.rationale: A parked repo is the natural state — object-store bytes plus KV rows, no per-share process to wind down and no wake ceremony; first touch pays only auth + cached repo lookup and pyramid sstable fetches (single-flight download then disk-persistent cache, pkg/pyramid/tier_fs.go:342-455), and the whole server tier is stateless enough to scale on demand. Deductions: the shared KV database bills whether or not any repo is touched, and deleted/uncommitted garbage on parked repos accrues in the object store until the operator runs the external Spark GC (design/accepted/gc_plus/uncommitted-gc.md:178-183).
cells.vs_lean: A point above Lean's 3.5: Lean needs hibernation machinery per share; lakeFS repos have nothing to hibernate, so parking is free by construction.

verdicts.reason: Every citation checks out: cmd/lakefs/cmd/run.go:89-98 logger.Fatal on kv.Open/ValidateSchemaVersion; pkg/httputil/endpoints.go:16-23 static 'alive!'; pkg/kv/dynamodb/store.go:601-609 health Check() logs Debug only; pkg/graveler/staging/manager.go:78-99 staged entries are single kv.GetMsg records; grep of esti/*_test.go for restart/chaos = 0. Adversarial probes support 4: uploads are durable-before-ack (upload.WriteBlob to the block adapter at pkg/api/controller.go:3600 precedes the KV pointer), the second /healthcheck endpoint (controller.go:2189) is also a bare 204 so no hidden KV-aware probe exists, and no hang path was found — failures surface as HTTP errors. The fleet-wide KV blast radius (refs, auth, staged pointers) is real and correctly priced as the deduction from 5.

Citations verified: SetIf CAS contract pkg/kv/store.go:96-100; lakefs migrate up + DoMigration cmd/lakefs/cmd/migrate.go:129-159 (currently trivial — only a schema-version bump); gracefulShutdownTimeout=30s run.go:48; pyramid handleExistingFiles rescan pkg/pyramid/tier_fs.go:110-147; gateway multiparts in KV partition 'multiparts' pkg/gateway/multipart/tracker.go:13; CHANGELOG.md has exactly 249 '## v' releases (v0.8.1→v1.86.0). A probe strengthened the cell: an instance dying mid-async-task does not wedge it — pkg/catalog/catalog.go:2908-2935 detects the missing instance heartbeat and marks the task stale/retryable. Zero in-repo restart e2e legs is a fair quibble but the architecture (all durable state in KV/object store, CAS everywhere, stateless replicas) plus the 249-release record leaves no code evidence against 4.5.

Verified: per-instance (not per-repo) 5s TaskHeartbeatInterval written only while tasks are active (pkg/catalog/catalog.go:88-89, 2292-2296); branch_ownership.enabled=false default (pkg/config/defaults.go:171) and MostlyCorrectOwner explicitly correctness-optional (pkg/distributed/mc_owner.go:18-46); server only writes GC prepare listings under _lakefs/retention (pkg/graveler/retention/garbage_collection_manager.go:22-27); mark/sweep is the external Spark job (clients/spark/src/main/scala/io/treeverse/gc/GarbageCollection.scala) with the design doc's ~3h bottom line for a 20M-object repo (design/accepted/gc_plus/uncommitted-gc.md:206-213). Zero per-repo standing compute vs the Spark+operated-KV counterweight lands correctly at 4 vs Lean 3.5.

Verified and slightly reinforced: API metrics labeled only {operationID, statusCode} (pkg/api/metrics_middleware.go:28-33), gateway only {operation, code} (pkg/gateway/stats.go:14), and an independent repo-wide grep found no repository-labeled Prometheus metric anywhere in pkg. Both health endpoints are static — /_health 'alive!' (pkg/httputil/endpoints.go:16-23) and /healthcheck bare 204 (pkg/api/controller.go:2189-2191, swagger 'check that the API server is up') — so a dead-KV replica passes probes. Audit fields are gated on IsAdvancedAuth, hardwired false in OSS BasicAuthService (pkg/auth/basic_service.go:49-51; defaults.go:76 rbac 'none'); stats.enabled=true telemetry goes to the vendor (defaults.go:126). Per-repo cleanliness only via per-repo DiffBranch (controller.go:3448). 2.5 under Lean's 3 is right.

Verified: one listener dispatches per-request between S3 gateway (Host match or AWS signature) and API (cmd/lakefs/cmd/run.go:286-297), so any stock S3 SDK works with zero client install; lakectl local ships seven subcommands (cmd/lakectl/cmd/local_checkout.go, local_clone.go, local_commit.go, local_init.go, local_list.go, local_pull.go, local_status.go) in one unprivileged binary; presign upload/download paths exist (pkg/api/helpers/upload.go:382-419 incl. Azure BlockBlob handling); PreSignSupportMultipart is set only by the S3 adapter (pkg/block/s3/adapter.go:921), confirming the stated variance. Nothing privileged, no kernel module, no CSI — 4.5 above Lean's 3.5 is justified, with the enterprise Everest mount correctly excluded.

Verified: a parked repo is object-store bytes plus KV rows with no per-repo process (no standing per-repo objects found anywhere; heartbeats only run with active tasks, catalog.go:2292-2296); first touch pays a fast-path local open or a download into the disk-persistent pyramid cache (pkg/pyramid/tier_fs.go:342-360 openOrDownload, cacheAccess Hit path), and the cache re-registers across restarts (tier_fs.go:110-147). Deductions are real: the shared KV bills regardless, and uncommitted/deleted garbage on parked repos accrues until the external Spark GC runs (design/accepted/gc_plus/uncommitted-gc.md:171-183 run-report flow, Limitations). Nothing to hibernate and no wake ceremony — 4.5 vs Lean's 3.5 stands.

findings.detail: The lakeFS column is a max() over two mutually exclusive postures, while flint was deliberately disaggregated into per-front-end columns (sys/krb5p/FUSE/Lean) so each posture prices coherently. Performance 'Hot-loop local I/O' 5 and 'Cold start' 3 are earned by the lakectl-local face (plain local files, no process on the I/O path — /private/tmp/claude-503/-Users-ddalton-github-flint/f57a231a-2ffd-4e81-9c84-89a5317dadfc/scratchpad/lakefs/pkg/local/sync.go, index.go), but Consistency 'Acked-write crash durability' 4.5, 'Read freshness' 3.5, and 'Multi-writer arbitration' 3.5 are earned by the API/gateway face. No single workload gets both: an agent hot-looping sqlite on a lakectl-local checkout has bare-local-file durability until push — the exact fact that scored Lean 1.5 — and snapshot-until-sync freshness (~Lean's 1.5), while an API-face workload has hot-loop ~1.5 (2-3 HTTPS RTs/op). In flint's rubric FUSE's hot-loop 4 co-lives with FUSE's durability 1.5 in the SAME column; lakeFS gets the good half of two columns. The lakectl-local durability hole is currently hidden inside a shared 0.5 deduction bundled with single-node badger.
findings.suggested_fix: Either split lakeFS into two columns ('server API/gateway' and 'lakectl local') matching flint's per-front-end structure, or annotate the four affected cells with which face earns them and state the envelope caveat in the report header. If one column must stand, the durability/freshness cells should carry an explicit 'API face only; lakectl-local checkouts are Lean-grade here' footnote.

findings.detail: pkg/actions (6.4k LOC, in the package map) was examined by zero dimensions despite being default-on and load-bearing. Verified: actions.enabled=true and actions.env.enabled=true (env prefix LAKEFSACTION_) by default (pkg/config/defaults.go:62-64); pre-commit/pre-merge hooks run synchronously inside the graveler commit path (pkg/graveler/graveler.go:2314, 3348); webhooks POST to arbitrary hook-author-chosen URLs from the server's network position (authenticated SSRF: cloud metadata endpoints, internal services) with a hook-author-controlled timeout parsed from hook properties with no visible cap (pkg/actions/webhook.go:27, 60-67, default 1m) — so any principal with write access (all-repo in OSS ACL mode) can stall or veto every commit on a branch and make the server issue requests. The Lua runtime runs server-side with crypto/storage/formats modules (pkg/actions/lua/open.go:37-58); mitigations verified: net/http is gated behind actions.lua.net_http_enabled defaulting false (open.go:59, no viper default set), and Lua cloud clients require caller-supplied static creds, not the server's (lua/storage/aws/s3.go:26). This bears on Security (tenancy/blast-radius/SSRF), Day-2 Failure shape (a synchronous external dependency inside the commit path — currently scored 4 on 'no hang path was found'), and Consistency arbitration (programmable refusal is an unpriced positive).
findings.suggested_fix: Add an actions/hooks paragraph to the report. Re-examine Day-2 Failure shape 4 in light of writer-controlled synchronous webhooks in the commit path (likely still 4 with the caveat stated), and note the SSRF surface plus its real mitigations (Lua net/http default-off, no server-credential inheritance) in the Security dimension note rather than adjusting the already-low tenancy 1.5.

findings.detail: The Security note ('real SigV4/OIDC authentication') and the Client-authentication verdict cite the API chain covering 'jwt/basic/cookie/oidc/saml' as support for 3.5, but pkg/auth/build.go:16-27 (verified) Fatals any non-basic auth mode unless an external auth API service is configured — the pattern served by lakeFS Enterprise's auth service, not by anything in this repo. Shipped OSS is basic mode (single superAdmin, MaxUsers=1) full stop; the OIDC/SAML middleware code is present but unreachable without the enterprise-side component. The 3.5 itself survives on per-request SigV4 with static keys (a real half-point over Lean's static bearer), but part of its stated rationale rests on capability not exercisable from this repo.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep 3.5 but rewrite the rationale and dimension note to rest on SigV4 per-request signing alone; move OIDC/SAML to the 'enterprise deltas' sentence alongside per-repo RBAC and mount. Also surface the legacy SigV2/HMAC-SHA1 acceptance the verdict found but did not price.

findings.detail: Evidence-standard asymmetry on Day-2: flint's Lean 3.5s are drill-proven numbers (the flint scoring ethos requires observed behavior), while lakeFS's above-Lean 4/4.5 cells rest on architectural inference the verdicts themselves undercut — 'grep of esti for restart/chaos = 0', migration machinery 'currently trivial — only a schema-version bump', and the 249-release CHANGELOG record cited as a proxy for restart safety. Upgrades & restart recovery 4.5 is the highest Day-2 score in the whole table and is the least directly evidenced cell in it. Scoring lakeFS on architecture while flint was scored on drills systematically favors the system that was not tested.
findings.suggested_fix: Either trim Upgrades & restart recovery 4.5 to 4 (parity-plus with Lean, reflecting stateless-replica architecture minus zero in-repo restart evidence), or add an explicit 'evidence basis' marker per Day-2 cell (drill-proven vs architecture-inferred) so the 4.5 is legible as an inference.

findings.detail: Two facts are each priced on their home axis and then re-counted in the Misconfiguration-resistance adjustment to 2.5: the cleartext-default 0.0.0.0:8000 listener already costs Wire protection its half-point below Lean (3.5), and the unauthenticated /metrics + /_pprof mount already anchors Unauthenticated DoS at 2.5; both then reappear as two of the 'four independent silent-insecure defaults' justifying misconfig 3→2.5. The genuinely new fact in the adjustment — the OVERRIDE_THIS_SIGNING_SECRET_DEFAULT HMAC constant binding in all modes with only a non-empty check (pkg/config/defaults.go:23,107) — plus the triple-duty symmetric secret is sufficient on its own to carry the half-point.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the adjusted 2.5 but rest it on the signing-secret default and the triple-duty secret; cite the cleartext listener and pprof mount as cross-references to the axes where they are already priced, not as additional deductions.

findings.detail: CAS / conditional-write fidelity has a half-point grade inversion against the axis's own 'detection vs refusal' clause: lakeFS's implemented conditional primitive is refusal-grade — the KV insert-if-absent arbitrates the race itself (pkg/graveler/staging/manager.go:117-136), verified by the adversary — while flint Lean's 4 rests on the v1.30.0 ETag/If-Match machinery that is NFS-VERIFY-based detection, explicitly 'detection NOT serialisation, weakest under load' (and Lean's per-request epoch enforcement is not yet built at HEAD). lakeFS is docked 0.5 for missing If-Match vocabulary despite its present primitive being of a stronger enforcement grade than the machinery that earned Lean its 4.
findings.suggested_fix: Either raise lakeFS to 4 (vocabulary gap offset by refusal-grade enforcement), or state explicitly in the rubric that vocabulary breadth outweighs enforcement grade on this axis — and then note that Lean's 4 includes detection-grade and partially unbuilt enforcement, so the comparison reads honestly.

headlines: lakeFS beats flint Lean exactly where the server owns the truth: an acked write is already in S3 plus the KV store before the app sees success (4.5 vs 1.5), API readers see each other's staged writes immediately (3.5 vs 1.5), and branch/merge machinery genuinely arbitrates concurrent writers with per-key conflict refusal (3.5 vs 2.5) — the structural reason is that lakeFS replaced the filesystem with a KV-CAS-serialized commit store rather than caching one.

Everything filesystem-shaped inverts: no locks, no rename, no shared sqlite/git across clients (1.5), metadata storms pay 2-3 HTTPS round-trips per file against Lean's local-NVMe 5, and every POSIX workload requires a full local copy the repo's own CLI warns is non-scalable — the mount that would fix this ('Everest', NFS/FUSE write mode) is enterprise and not in this codebase.

On out-of-band writes the two systems are exact mirrors: Lean preserves and surfaces foreign writes via its inbox (4), while lakeFS hides them, schedules them for GC deletion, or serves a foreign overwrite corrupt under an unverified stored ETag (1) — the object store is lakeFS's private heap, not a shared surface.

Read the lakeFS column with one caveat: it is an envelope of two postures no single workload gets at once — the durability and freshness scores belong to the API/gateway face, while the hot-loop-5 and cold-start scores belong to lakectl-local checkouts, whose plain local files have Lean-grade (not 4.5-grade) durability until pushed.

As a fleet citizen lakeFS is cheaper than Lean on nearly every Day-2 axis — stateless replicas, a parked repo is just KV rows plus bytes, clients get HTTP errors instead of wedged mounts — but OSS multi-tenancy is where the enterprise split bites hardest: the shipped build is one superAdmin or all-repo grants (tenancy 1.5 vs 4), with a default-on hooks engine that puts writer-authored webhooks synchronously inside the commit path.
